newsitem.title: UK: US holiday gasoline demand helps oil price higher.
newsitem.headline: US holiday gasoline demand helps oil price higher.

text.p: Summer holiday demand for gasoline in the United States helped world oil prices higher again on Thursday despite an imminent wave of Iraqi crude exports.
Tight U.S. gasoline markets helped add 20 cents to the price of North Sea Brent blend crude taking it to $19.19 a barrel at the close of London futures trade.
Dealers said an outage of Exxon's Baytown, Texas gasoline-making catalytic cracking unit had helped lend support to U.S. gasoline futures and encouraged further speculative buying.
Gasoline is in unexpectedly short supply in the United States because demand has risen faster than anticipated this year.
Weekly oil inventory data released on Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute for the week ended August 8 showed U.S. gasoline stocks near historical lows for the time of year.
Traders said buoyant U.S. gasoline prices were tempting cargoes transatlantic from the tight European market.
Nigeria, one of the world's biggest crude producers, is also expected to add to its recent run of gasoline purchases making up for poor supplies from mismanaged refineries.
Oil also found support earlier on Thursday from news of a lower programme of loadings scheduled for the North Sea pipeline system in September.
Traders said they had been notified of a 35.5-cargo programme, down three cargoes from August.
Capping price rises are renewed Iraqi crude exports under the stage of the United Nations' oil-for-food exchange and sales of crude from German strategic stocks.
